## Reviewer's guide v1 — not for the author

> [!TIP]
> **This is the reviewer's guide.** Work through the ⚠️ checklist below, then approve — **approving asserts only that the ⚠️ items looked right to you.** Machine-verified this run: links, shortcodes, page metadata, and every claim marked verified (receipts on the evidence page). Code samples are read, not compiled.
>
> _PR author: your to-do list is the other review comment, "Author action guide" — nothing on this card is yours._

> [!NOTE]
> **What this PR changes:**
>
> - The Cloud REST API schema content adapter now sets `sitemap_exclude` on every page it generates (~800 pages), removing them from `sitemap.xml`.
> - A long comment above the `$params` dict records why the sitemap was trimmed instead of marking the pages `noindex`.
>
> Nothing here changes page content, so the wrongness that would matter is mechanical or strategic: a flag the sitemap template doesn't honor, or an SEO decision the team doesn't want. The review read the changed template, confirmed the flag's handling in the sitemap layout, and checked that no indexability directive was introduced.
>
> **Review confidence:**
>
> | Dimension | Level | Notes |
> | :--- | :---: | :--- |
> | mechanics | HIGH |  |
> | facts | HIGH | Template change only — no reader-facing factual claims added. |

### ⚠️ Check these before approving

| | ID | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F?** | `content/docs/reference/cloud-rest-api/schema/_content.gotmpl` L120 | This drops roughly 800 URLs from `sitemap.xml` in one change — a site-wide search decision, not a page edit. The flag works as intended (the sitemap layout skips pages carrying it, and nothing here adds a `noindex`), so the only open question is whether the team wants this trade. Worth noting alongside it: our own contributor guide describes `sitemap_exclude` narrowly, as being for pages whose canonical URL is submitted in a *different* sitemap; this PR uses it for crawl-budget trimming instead. Confirm the stance, and decide whether that guidance should be widened to match. |
